verifications.claim: Seals and Crofts is an American soft rock duo.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'American soft rock duo Seals and Crofts.' R3: 'Genre Soft rock[1]' R2: 'duo Seals & Crofts'
verifications.reasoning: Directly described as American soft rock duo in R4; supported as duo and soft rock in R2/R3.

verifications.claim: Seals and Crofts consists of Jim Seals and Dash Crofts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'half of the duo Seals & Crofts alongside Jim Seals.' R3/R4: 'Songwriter(s) Jim Seals, Dash Crofts'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly names Jim Seals and Dash Crofts as the duo members across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: "Summer Breeze" was written by Seals and Crofts in 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R4: 'Songwriter(s) Jim Seals, Dash Crofts' 'Released August 1972'. R2: 'the 1972 track “Summer Breeze”'
verifications.reasoning: Credited to Seals and Crofts with 1972 release date directly stated.

verifications.claim: "Summer Breeze" was originally recorded by Seals and Crofts in 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: '1972 song by American soft rock duo Seals and Crofts... Released August 1972'. R3: '1972 song by American duo Seals and Crofts'. R1: 'Seals and Crofts’ hit “Summer Breeze.” Culled from the album of the same name'
verifications.reasoning: Identified as original recording by Seals and Crofts in 1972; R1 notes early covers after their version.

verifications.claim: "Summer Breeze" peaked at No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'reached No. 6 on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart'. R3: 'number 6 in... the United States'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states peak of No. 6 on Billboard Hot 100 for Seals and Crofts' version.

verifications.claim: The Isley Brothers covered "Summer Breeze" in 1974.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'In 1974, The Isley Brothers covered Summer Breeze... Released March 1974'. R4: 'covered... as a single in 1974. Issued also on their 1973 album'. R1: 'one of the first covers... Isley Brothers'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly covered/released as single in 1974; album in 1973 but claim specifies cover in 1974.

verifications.claim: Type O Negative released a metal version of "Summer Breeze" in 1993.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Type O Negative released a cover... in August 1993 on their album Bloody Kisses... Genre Gothic metal... Recorded 1993'. R1: 'covered... to Type O Negative'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states 1993 release on album, gothic metal genre (metal version), cover confirmed.
